stem: Which of the following is the solution set of the inequality \(\frac{x}{2} - \frac{x - 3}{5} > 2\)?
solution: Divide by 3 (positive, so the sign stays): \(x > \frac{14}{3}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This distributes the \(-2\) as \(-2x - 6\); the correct product is \(-2x + 6\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This adds the \(x\)-terms, \(5x + 2x\), instead of subtracting \(2x\) from \(5x\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. Dividing by the positive number 3 does not reverse the inequality sign.

verify:
P = lambda s: value(s.replace('\\le', '<=').replace('\\ge', '>='))
x = symbols('x')
s = solve_univariate_inequality(x/2 - (x - 3)/5 > 2, x, relational=False)
assert s == Interval.open(Rational(14, 3), oo)
assert solve_univariate_inequality(P(choices[answer]), x, relational=False) == s
assert all(solve_univariate_inequality(P(choices[k]), x, relational=False) != s for k in choices if k != answer)
